item.title: Ohio Rep Marcy Kaptur hospitalized after hit-and-run crash on way to church
item.description: Rep. Marcy Kaptur was hospitalized after a hit-and-run car crash near Toledo, Ohio, while traveling to church Sunday morning. Her office said she suffered injuries that are not life-threatening.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Marcy Kaptur, D-Ohio, was hospitalized Sunday morning after the vehicle she was riding in was struck in a hit-and-run crash that also injured her driver, according to the Toledo Police Department. 

Kaptur was on her way to church when the wreck happened near Toledo, her office said in a statement.

She suffered injuries that are not life-threatening and remain in stable condition.

"This morning, Congresswoman Kaptur was a passenger in a vehicle on her way to a church service when the car she was traveling in was struck. She is active, alert, and being treated for non-life threatening injuries," her office said.

FAKE COP SUSPECTED IN LAWMAKER ASSASSINATION HAD EXTENSIVE SECURITY TRAINING BEFORE 'TARGETED' ATTACK

The driver of the vehicle Kaptur was traveling in was identified as Kegan Zimmermann, who was also taken to a nearby hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, authorities said.

Police told Fox News Digital the "hit-skip crash" happened at about 10:48 a.m. local time at the intersection of North Detroit and Central avenues.

"A vehicle traveling southbound came into the path of Representative Kaptur, causing a collision. Both Representative Kaptur and Mr. Zimmerman were transported to St. Vincent's medical center for undisclosed, yet not serious injuries," police said in a statement. 

"The driver of the at-fault vehicle fled the scene."

Both vehicles involved were impounded as evidence is being collected and processed.

The investigation remains in its early stages, police said.

"Toledo Police investigators have made significant progress and continue to follow several strong leads as they work to identify the driver responsible," authorities said. 

Toledo Police Chief Michael Troendle added that he has been in touch with Kaptur and was pleased to hear she was recovering.

"I had a chance to speak with Representative Marcy Kaptur today, and we're glad to hear she's doing well. Our thoughts remain with her and Mr. Zimmermann as they recover," Troendle said in a statement. "Our investigators continue to make progress on this case. I appreciate the work our investigators have put in today, as well as the cooperation we've received from members of the community. We're committed to identifying the person responsible and ensuring they are held accountable."

FORMER WISCONSIN JUDGE HANNAH DUGAN AVOIDS JAIL TIME FOR OBSTRUCTING ARREST OF ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT

In a statement posted on X, Kaptur praised the police and fire departments for their quick response to the scene.

"We look forward to additional information from Toledo Police as they investigate the accident," the statement read. 

"Congresswoman Kaptur is thankful for the quick actions of first responders from Toledo Police and Fire Departments who arrived promptly on scene, and the medical professionals helping to take care of those involved in the crash."

Hundreds of Kaptur’s constituents reportedly reached out to the congresswoman following the incident.

"She expressed her deep gratitude to the hundreds of constituents who have reached out and looks forward to returning to a full schedule soon," her office said. 

Fox News Digital reached out to the Toledo Fire & Rescue for more information.

item.title: Entire Squad endorses Abdul El-Sayed days before Michigan Democratic Senate primary
item.description: Every Squad member has endorsed Abdul El-Sayed in the Michigan Senate primary, even as he distances himself from the Democratic Socialists of America.
item.content:encoded:
Every member of the "Squad," an informal left-wing congressional caucus, has endorsed Abdul El-Sayed ahead of Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary, according to his campaign website.

The Squad is made up of Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., Ayanna Pressley, D-Mass., Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich., Summer Lee, D-Pa., Delia Ramirez, D-Ill., and Greg Casar, D-Texas.

Many of the squad’s current and former members have past or ongoing affiliations with the Democratic Socialists of America, an organization El-Sayed is attempting to distance himself from as he attempts to moderate ahead of a swing-state general election.

The unified endorsements sharpen the ideological stakes of the Tuesday primary, linking El-Sayed to the party’s most prominent progressive bloc even as he rejects the socialist label and seeks to present himself as a viable candidate in a battleground state. The support also gives Republicans an early line of attack should El-Sayed defeat the more centrist Stevens and advance to the general election.

DEM PRIMARY ERUPTS AS ESTABLISHMENT FAVORITE DISMISSES RIVAL AS ‘CELEBRITY CANDIDATE’

"The entire Squad has now endorsed Abdul El-Sayed to carry on its radical, socialist, anti-American agenda in the U.S. Senate, and they will be rejected by Michiganders at the ballot box," National Republican Senatorial Committee regional press secretary Samantha Cantrell told Fox News Digital.

Casar was the most recent Squad member to endorse El-Sayed, throwing his support behind him Thursday.

"Abdul El-Sayed is showing what it means to run a bold, pro-working class campaign," Casar said. "House progressives need strong partners in the Senate in order to put money in your pocket, get money out of politics, and win Medicare for All. I’m proud to endorse Abdul."

SOCIALIST-BACKED DEM WHO RIPPED THE WEALTHY CRACKS STATE’S TOP 1%, TAX RETURNS SHOW

Casar, Ocasio-Cortez, Tlaib and Lee all have current or former Democratic Socialists of America affiliations. El-Sayed at one point even appeared at a Democratic Socialists of America event alongside Tlaib.

El-Sayed headlined that event, a fundraiser that brought in roughly $10,000 for the Detroit Democratic Socialists of America, and was photographed next to Tlaib behind a table with a poster on it depicting a hand labeled "DSA" choking a snake labeled "capitalism."

The Michigan Senate hopeful attended and spoke at six Democratic Socialists of America events between 2017 and 2020, Fox News Digital previously reported. Organizers affiliated with the socialist organization have described El-Sayed as "a longtime friend of Detroit DSA."

ABDUL EL-SAYED SAYS RALLYING WITH HASAN PIKER DOESN'T MEAN HE ENDORSES 'AMERICA DESERVED 9/11' REMARK

Despite pulling in endorsements from socialists and his longtime association with the Democratic Socialists of America, El-Sayed rejects the socialist label and has distanced himself from the group.

"I'm not technically or practically DSA," El-Sayed told The Wall Street Journal in early July.

In an interview with CNN, he said, "I am not somebody who is a socialist. I believe in capitalism, I just believe that capitalism has to be regulated."

El-Sayed faces off against Rep. Haley Stevens in Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary Tuesday. Stevens is widely viewed as the more centrist of the two. Polls generally show El-Sayed leading Stevens by a comfortable margin, according to the New York Times.

The El-Sayed campaign did not respond to a request for comment.
